headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors from OpenHands into unstructured; shared writable files and broad egress make the pair unsafe by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write runtime files and use MCP; unstructured reads documents and writes files. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if OpenHands ingests unstructured outputs from a shared workspace. The pair is not provably isolated, but the interaction is not documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF OpenHands reads unstructured-produced files as instructions in the shared runtime volume
IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Add a manual review step before OpenHands acts on parsed content
Use read-only mounts for unstructured outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches mounted runtime files and can send data to a user-configured model provider; unstructured processes documents, images, and text. If sensitive documents are placed in the shared workspace, both agents can access them and OpenHands may transmit context externally. The profiles do not prove a leak, but the default pathway exists.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are mounted into the shared runtime volume
IF OpenHands is configured with an external model provider while processing those documents
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use a local-only model provider for OpenHands
Restrict unstructured to a separate input directory
Redact documents before processing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and read the filesystem, and OpenHands also modifies git state. In a shared mounted volume, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git history without locking. This is a default-dangerous overlap because the profiles show no coordination primitive or lock manager.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory
IF either agent writes to git-tracked files without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write access with a simple operator lock
Pause one agent while the other commits
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate edits and actions from its agent loop, while unstructured produces parsed document outputs. If unstructured output is treated as authoritative input, OpenHands may act on incorrect extractions and propagate errors into files or git state. The pair lacks documented verification between them, so I escalate to high.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes unstructured output without a verification step
IF the downstream action is a file edit or git commit based on extracted text
mitigations: Require human review of extracted fields
Compare extracted values against source documents
Limit OpenHands to draft-only changes
Keep unstructured outputs in a staging folder
requires-engineering: add schema validation before action

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so no specific compliance breach is proven. However, OpenHands can egress to a configured model provider while unstructured handles documents and images, so a compliance gap could arise if regulated documents are processed. I cite both because the risk depends on their combined handling.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through the shared workflow
IF OpenHands sends those documents or derived context to an external provider
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Use a residency-approved provider
Document retention settings before use
Separate compliance-sensitive workloads
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement
